# Page 16^page=16
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS Overview of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 Held in New Delhi The inaugural edition of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit (BRES) & Expo 2026 was held under the theme of “Invest. Innovate. Inspire” from November 2 to 5, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Delhi. • The summit was inaugurated by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi and concluded with a valedictory address delivered by Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan. • The summit was held alongside the 9th session of the International Solar Alliance (ISA) assembly and the 4th International Conference on Green Hydrogen (ICGH). Exam Hints: ✓ What? BRES & Expo 2026 ✓ Edition: 1st ✓ Venue: Bharat Mandapam (New Delhi, Delhi) ✓ Theme: “Invest Innovate Inspire” ✓ Inaugurated by: PM Narendra Modi ✓ Total Investments Secured: USD 400 billion across RE sector ✓ Agreements Signed: 10 MoUs and framework agreements ✓ Reports and Platforms Released: 37 ✓ Major MoU: SECI–Power2X for green methanol supply ✓ Key Events: 9th ISA Assembly and 4th ICGH. About BRES & Expo 2026: Participants: The summit attracted over 75,000 visitors from 135 countries, with 400+ exhibitors, 620+ speakers and 113 sessions. It also witnessed participation from 32+ international ministers, 8 partner countries and the European Union (EU), along with 14 partner States and Union Territories (UTs), 6 Chief Ministers (CMs) and 10 State Energy Ministers. Organised by: The four-day summit was organised by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) in partnership with the ISA, with the Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA) and Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) serving as organising partners. Country Partners: The summit featured 8 partner countries: Australia, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom (UK), along with the European Union (EU) as a partner. Key Address: PM Narendra Modi announced plans to add another 500 gigawatts (GW) of non-fossil fuel capacity over the next 10–11 years, highlighting India’s achievement of 50% non-fossil fuel installed power capacity in 2025, five years ahead of schedule. • While addressing the summit, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi, MNRE, highlighted that over the last 10 years, India’s Renewable Energy sector has attracted over Rs 15 lakh crore in investment, of which nearly Rs 6 lakh crore had flowed into the sector in just the last two years. Key Address by VP: The Vice-President of India, C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the valedictory session of the summit, where he highlighted India’s achievements in the Renewable Energy (RE) sector, its commitment to sustainable development and the transformative role of clean energy in empowering households, farmers and communities across the country. • Installed Electricity Capacity from Non-fossil Sources: India’s non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity capacity had breached 300 GigaWatt (GW). In addition, the country reached 50% share

# Page 17^page=17
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 17 Daily Content PDF of the installed electricity capacity from non-fossil sources in 2025, surpassing its original target of 5 years. • Surge in Solar Capacity: Further, India’s solar capacity had increased from less than 3 GW to over 170 GW over the last years. • Grassroots-level Engagement: Over 65 lakh households had joined the solar movement under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSGMBY); and nearly 30 lakh farmers had benefited under Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM). Key Outcomes: Total Investment Commitments: At the summit, India secured the investment commitments worth nearly USD 400 billion across the RE sector, which is almost double the USD 220 billion investment estimated by the Government of India (GoI) to fund the country’s green energy transition by 2030. Total MoUs: The summit witnessed the signing of 10 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and framework agreements covering technology, research, manufacturing and renewable energy development. • Among them, the Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) signed an MoU with Netherlands-based Power2X to facilitate the international supply of green molecules, including a proposed initial supply of 3 lakh tonnes of green methanol annually. MoUs by Odisha Government: At the BRES & Expo 2026, the Government of Odisha signed 18 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) worth Rs 1.17 lakh crore for clean and RE projects, with a proposed capacity addition of 11, 742 Mega-Watt (MW). • The state government targets to become one of the top 5 power-exporting states in India and source 74% of its installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2047. Release of Report: The summit witnessed the launch of International Energy Agency’s (IEA) report titled “India RE Market Report 2026: Analysis and Forecast to 2030”. Some of the key findings of the report are: • Utility-scale Solar Generation Cost: India’s utility-scale solar generation cost reached USD 30– 35 per Mega-Watt-hour (MWh) (Rs 2,840-Rs 3,313), the lowest in the world that had helped India to save over USD 100 billion in fossil fuel imports, equivalent to approximately Rs 9.46 lakh crore. • Solar Module Manufacturing Capacity: India’s solar module manufacturing capacity surpassed 225 Giga-Watt (GW) in September 2026, which makes India the world’s second-largest manufacturer of solar modules. • Auction of RE projects: So far, India auctioned 15 GW of hybrid Renewable Energy (RE) projects, bringing the total auctioned capacity to 64 GW. • Average Tariffs: between 2023 and 2025, the average tariffs stood at around USD 45 per MWh (Rs 4,260), which was 20% below the average cost of electricity from coal-fired power plants. ISA Initiatives: The ISA proposed a USD 200 million Africa Solar Facility and launched the ISA Academy and Global Capability Centre–SHINE (Strategic Hub for Innovation and Execution or Strategic Network for Innovation and Execution) to promote solar financing, training and capacity building. • It also plans to deploy 1 million solar pumps globally, facilitate 500 megawatts (MW) of solar capacity across Small Island Developing States (SIDS) by 2030, and expand the SUNRISE Network to 35 countries.

# Page 18^page=18
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF About Ministry of New & Renewable Energy (MNRE): Union Minister- Pralhad Joshi (Constituency- Dharwad, Karnataka) Minister of State (MoS)- Shripad Yesso Naik (Rajya Sabha- North Goa, Goa) MoSPI’s ASI 2024–25: 5 States, including TN, Karnataka, Contributed Over 54% of India’s Total manufacturing GVA in FY25 In November 2026, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) released the results of Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) for the reference period April 2024 to March 2025 i.e. Financial Year 2024-25 (FY25), including Volume I and Summary Results of Factory Sector along with unit level data . • The data showed that 5 states namely, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu (TN), Karnataka, and Uttar Pradesh (UP) , contributed over 54% of India’s total manufacturing Gross Value Added (GVA) in FY25. • The manufacturing corporate sector registered 9.28% growth in GVA, while India’s overall registered manufacturing GVA grew by 9.59% during FY25. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of ASI results for FY25 ✓ Released by: MoSPI ✓ Reference Period: April 2024–March 2025 ✓ Survey Period: October 2025–June 2026 ✓ Combined GVA Share: Over 54% ✓ Manufacturing GVA Growth: 9.59% ✓ Top 5 States: Maharashtra, Gujarat, TN, Karnataka and UP (over 54% of India’s manufacturing GVA) ✓ Top 5 Sectors (Employment): Food products; textiles; basic metals; motor vehicles, and wearing apparel (more than 41% of total manufacturing employment). About ASI for FY25: Source: The MoSPI collected the data for ASI from the selected factories under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 as amended in 2017 and Rules framed there under in 2011, through a dedicated web portal using an establishment-based approach. Data: The latest survey presented data relating to capital, employment, emoluments and several other economic parameters relevant to the industrial sector like: number of factories; fixed/working capital; total input; total output; depreciation; GVA; employment details and fuels consumption details, among others. Coverage: The latest survey has covered: registered factories, bidi and cigar establishments, certain electricity undertakings and eligible establishments with minimum 100 employees included in state business registers. Key Findings: Manufacturing GVA: The manufacturing corporate sector (which accounted for over 89% of total GVA) registered a growth rate of 9.28% in terms of GVA in FY25, while the number of factories in operation and total employment increased by 3.45% and 7.57%, respectively. • The registered manufacturing sector witnessed growth in capital investment, industrial output, GVA, employment and wages compared to the previous year. Additionally, GVA per person engaged increased by 2.25%, while the gross value of plant and machinery rose by 7.25%.

About Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI): Minister of State (MoS)(Independent Charge, IC)-Rao Inderjit Singh (Constituency- Gurugram, Haryana) Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Launches ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’ to Strengthen Intergenerational Bonding In November 2026, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE) launched the ‘Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan’, a National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign, under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) in New Delhi, Delhi. • The campaign aims to foster intergenerational solidarity while ensuring the dignity, care and social inclusion of senior citizens. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan. ✓ Nature: National Intergenerational Bonding Campaign. ✓ Launched by: Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment. ✓ Location: New Delhi. ✓ Scheme: Under Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY). ✓ Core Framework: 5C Model: Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue. ✓ Volunteer Initiative: Vayo SAATHI (Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion). Highlights of Vayo Samman Rashtriya Abhiyan: Framework: The campaign follows the 5C Model – Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue to strengthen intergenerational bonding through interaction, knowledge-sharing and sustained community participation.

Vayo SAATHI: Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar released the campaign handbook and launched Vayo SAATHI (Support, Awareness, Assistance, Training, Health and Inclusion), a digitally enabled volunteer initiative for citizens aged 18 years and above to support senior citizens. • Volunteers can register through the Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW) SAMAVESH Portal or JEEVAN (Joint Elderly Empowerment & Virtual Assistance Network) Application (App) and receive a Vayo SAATHI Certificate. Partnerships: Two MoUs were signed with Shri Ram Chandra Mission (SRCM) and Adhyatma Vigyan Satsang Kendra (AVSK), Jodhpur, Rajasthan to promote the holistic well-being of senior citizens through meditation, yoga, wellness programmes, community-based activities, intergenerational engagement, pledge drives and walkathons. About Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE): Union Minister – Dr. Virendra Kumar (Constituency – Tikamgarh, Madhya Pradesh (MP)) Minister of State (MoS) – Ram Das Athawale (Rajya Sabha – Maharashtra); Banwari Lal (B.L.) Verma (Rajya Sabha – Uttar Pradesh (UP)). Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman Released Rs. 250 Commemorative Coin Honouring Muthuswami Dikshitar In November 2026, Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, Ministry of Finance (MoF), released a Rs 250 commemorative coin to mark the 250th birth anniversary of Carnatic music maestro Muthuswami Dikshitar at Swatantrata Bhavan, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh (UP). • The coin was unveiled on 3 November 2026, at an event organised by the Centre of Excellence for Indian Knowledge Systems, Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), to honour Dikshitar’s contributions to Indian classical music. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Release of Commemorative Coin ✓ Released by: Union Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, MoF ✓ Honouring: 250th Birth Anniversary of Muthuswami Dikshitar ✓ Denomination: Rs 250 ✓ Weight: 35 Grams ✓ Diameter: 44 Millimetres ✓ Venue: Swatantrata Bhavan, IIT-BHU, Varanasi, UP. ✓ Support: BSE under its CSR initiative. ✓ Book Released: Amar Guruguham Potruvam. Highlights of the Commemorative Coin: Coin Issuance: The 35-gram commemorative coin, with a diameter of 44 mm, was minted at the India Government Mint, Mumbai, under the authority of the Central Government. It contains 50% silver (Ag), 40% copper (Cu), 5% nickel (Ni) and 5% zinc (Zn). Price and Availability: The collector’s coin was listed for sale at Rs 6,985, with 238 pieces shown in stock on 3 November 2026. It is intended as a commemorative collector’s item rather than for general cash transactions. Support: The event received Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) support from the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), with its Managing Director (MD) Sundararaman Ramamurthy associated with the initiative.

Legacy: Muthuswami Dikshitar, one of the Trinity of Carnatic Music alongside Tyagaraja and Syama Sastri, composed around 450–500 Sanskrit compositions dedicated largely to Hindu deities and temples, blending devotion and philosophy; his works remain an integral part of the Carnatic music repertoire. NITI Aayog and GIZ GmbH Sign Implementation Agreement under NDC-TIA II for Road Freight Decarbonisation On 3 November 2026, NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) and Germany’s Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH signed an Implementation Agreement under the Nationally Determined Contribution–Transport Initiative for Asia Phase II (NDC-TIA II) to accelerate the decarbonisation of India’s road freight sector. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Implementation Agreement for road freight decarbonisation ✓ Entities: NITI Aayog and GIZ GmbH (Germany) ✓ Initiative: NDC-TIA II ✓ Supported By: Germany’s International Climate Initiative (IKI) ✓ Implementing Partners: WRI India, ICCT India and Agora Energiewende ✓ Objective: Decarbonisation of India’s road freight sector ✓ Key Focus: Electrification of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles. About NDC-TIA II: Phase I: Launched in August 2020, NDC-TIA covered India, China and Vietnam, with support from Germany’s International Climate Initiative (IKI). • In India, NITI Aayog focused on transport decarbonisation, emission reduction and electric mobility. Focus: The NDC-TIA II is a regional initiative supported by the German Government’s International Climate Initiative (IKI), aimed at accelerating the decarbonisation of the transport sector, with a particular focus on road freight. Implementing Partners: The NDC-TIA II initiative is implemented in collaboration with World Resources Institute (WRI) India, International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) India, and Agora Energiewende. Key Focus Areas: The agreement promotes EV charging infrastructure, innovative financing and supportive regulations to accelerate freight decarbonisation and support India’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement, 2015. CSIR–DAKSHIN Sign LoA to Strengthen Global South Cooperation On 3 November 2026, the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Development and Knowledge Sharing Initiative (DAKSHIN) – Global South Centre of Excellence (CoE), hosted by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS), signed a Letter of Association (LoA) to promote capacity building, research collaboration and technology partnerships among countries of the Global South. • The LoA was signed by Dr. Rama Swami Bansal, Head of the International Science and Technology Affairs Directorate (ISTAD), CSIR, and Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General (DG), RIS. Exam Hints: ✓ What? LoA signed ✓ Organisations Involved: CSIR and DAKSHIN–Global South CoE ✓ Signatories: Dr. Rama Swami Bansal (CSIR) and Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma (RIS).

Ministry of Culture Sign MoU with Google Arts & Culture to Digitise India’s Cultural Heritage On 5 November 2026, the Ministry of Culture signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Google Arts & Culture to digitally preserve, document and showcase India’s cultural heritage using advanced digital technologies. • The MoU was signed at a virtual ceremony in the presence of Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, and Amit Sood, Vice President (VP) and Founder, Google Arts & Culture. Exam Hints: ✓ What? MoU signed ✓ Entities: Ministry of Culture and Google Arts & Culture ✓ Dignitaries: Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture; and Amit Sood, VP and Founder, Google Arts & Culture ✓ Objective: Digitisation, preservation and promotion of India’s cultural heritage through digital technologies ✓ Manuscript Initiative: Gyan Bharatam Mission ✓ Key Institutions: ASI, National Museum and NGMA ✓ Major Project: Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum. Key Areas of MoU: Objective: To use advanced digital technologies to preserve India’s historical monuments, archaeological sites, museum collections, manuscripts and traditional art forms. Heritage Digitisation: The collaboration will cover collections associated with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), National Museum and National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA). Gyan Bharatam: The initiative will support the digitisation and preservation of ancient manuscripts under the Gyan Bharatam initiative. Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum: The upcoming museum, located in the North and South Blocks, New Delhi, will be a major focus of the partnership, with digital documentation of its buildings and artefacts. MoMSME Signs MoU with TRIFED to Expand Market Access for Tribal Artisans under PM Vishwakarma Scheme In November 2026, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME) signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Tribal Cooperative Marketing Development Federation of India (TRIFED), under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA), to enhance market access for eligible tribal artisans registered under the Pradhan Mantri(PM) Vishwakarma Scheme.

Raman Institute: Founded the Raman Research Institute in Bengaluru, Karnataka, in 1948 and served as its director until 1970.
